headline: Robots worked as shop assistants and guides at tourist sites across China during the National Day holiday, as more than 30 robotics firms moved into tourism and retail this year.
score_reason: Pool score kept: robots working in public across China, but the figures are company-supplied and the article itself says the real test comes after the novelty fades.
importance_line: Visitors across China met robots selling goods and guiding tours, a large public test of whether such robots can pay their way, but the revenue figures come from the companies and the article itself says the real test is whether they still look worthwhile once the novelty fades.
summary: A report by the WeChat account Yuan Media Hub, published by 36Kr, says more than 30 robotics firms, meaning companies building robots that act in the physical world, have entered tourism and retail this year, with thousands of robots on duty at scenic spots during the holiday, and more than 300 robots at a theme park in Zhuhai that Agibot launched with Chimelong. It gives revenue figures from some robot stores, but also reports that a listed Chinese convenience-store operator paused a robot vending project after a year, and lists weak points such as grabbing errors on real shelves and the lack of repair services.
notes: Read from the pre-fetched full text. The article says it is from the WeChat official account Yuan Media Hub, written by Xie Chunsheng, and published with authorization from 36Kr, so the credit names both. Figures are company-supplied and not independently checked.
